lesson_title: Fuel That Falls From the Sky
hook_text: A filling station that never charges for petrol. South Africa owns one of the best on the planet — and the queue to use it starts now.
clip_script: Picture a filling station that never sends a bill for the petrol. You pay once — for the pumps, the pipes, the forecourt — and from then on the fuel simply arrives, every morning, free of charge, forever. That is the entire business case for non-conventional energy in one image: sunshine and wind cost nothing; only the catching machinery costs money. Coal must be dug, railed and burned afresh every day of its working life; a solar panel is bought once and then gathers free fuel for a quarter of a century. Name the catch immediately, because honesty scores. The free fuel keeps its own diary: the sun signs off at dusk, and the wind disappears without notice. So the free filling station needs either a storage tank or a reliable partner. Compress the trade-off into five words and keep them: free but moody, costly but steady. Now the nearly unfair part: South Africa's sky is one of the most generous on the planet. The Northern Cape banks over two thousand five hundred sunshine hours a year, while two oceans push dependable wind onto our coasts. Germany, under permanent grey cloud, became a solar superpower with about half our sunshine. The fuel was never our problem — the race is entirely about pumps. And the pumps are going in: more than a hundred plants stand already, and the auctions drove prices below new coal per unit. The free fuel turned out to be the cheap fuel as well.
visual_style: A cartoon filling station whose pump hose runs straight up into a beaming sun and a gusting cloud; a price board spinning down to zero; a split map glowing gold over the Northern Cape and streaked white with wind along the coasts; mirrors folding sunlight into a glowing thermos; a coal train fading as a price tag tips in favour of the panel.
mood: Bright, generous and quietly triumphant — the country that won the weather lottery.
pacing: Fast playful open at the free pump, steady build through the endowment, a crisp landing on the five-word trade-off.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and meet the three machines that catch the free fuel.
